column1: One of the most eminent of psychologists, Clark Hull, claimed that the essence of reasoning lies in the putting together of two ‘behaviour segments’ in some novel way, never actually performed before, so as to reach a goal.
column2: 著名心理学家克拉克·赫尔认为，推理的本质在于以某种前所未有的方式将两种‘行为片段’结合起来，从而达成某个目标。

column1: Two followers of Clark Hull, Howard and Tracey Kendler, devised a test for children that was explicitly based on Clark Hull’s principles.
column2: 克拉克·赫尔的两位追随者——霍华德和特蕾西·肯德勒，设计了一项专门针对儿童的测试，该测试明确基于克拉克·赫尔的理论原则进行设计。

column1: The children were given the task of learning to operate a machine so as to get a toy.
column2: 孩子们的任务就是学会操作这台机器，从而获得一个玩具。

column1: In order to succeed, they had to go through a two-stage sequence.
column2: 为了成功，他们必须经历一个两阶段的序列。

column1: The children were trained on each stage separately.
column2: 孩子们在每个阶段分别接受训练。

column1: The stages consisted merely of pressing the correct one of two buttons to get a marble; and of inserting the marble into a small hole to release the toy.
column2: 每个阶段仅包括按下两个按钮中的一个以获得一颗弹珠，然后将弹珠插入小孔以释放玩具。

column1: The Kendlers found that the children could learn the separate bits readily enough.
column2: 肯德尔发现孩子们能够轻松掌握各个部分。

column1: Given the task of getting a marble by pressing the button they could get the marble; given the task of getting a toy when a marble was handed to them, they could use the marble.
column2: 当任务要求他们通过按下按钮来获取弹珠时，他们就能够成功获得弹珠；而当弹珠被递给他们时，他们也可以利用这个弹珠来完成相应的任务。

column1: (All they had to do was put it in a hole.)
column2: 他们只需要把它放进一个洞里就行了。

column1: But they did not for the most part ‘integrate’, to use the Kendlers’ terminology.
column2: 但他们大部分并未‘综合’，用肯德尔的说法。

column1: They did not press the button to get the marble and then proceed without further help to use the marble to get the toy.
column2: 他们并没有按下按钮来获取弹珠，而是选择在没有其他帮助的情况下，利用弹珠来取得那个玩具。

column1: So the Kendlers concluded that they were incapable of deductive reasoning.
column2: 因此，肯德勒一家得出结论：他们不具备演绎推理的能力。

column1: The mystery at first appears to deepen when we learn, from another psychologist, Michael Cole, and his colleagues, that adults in an African culture apparently cannot do the Kendlers’ task either.
column2: 起初，当我们从另一位心理学家迈克尔·科尔及其同事那里得知，非洲文化中的成年人似乎也无法完成肯德尔任务时，这个谜题反而显得更加深奥。

column1: But it lessens, on the other hand, when we learn that a task was devised which was strictly analogous to the Kendlers’ one but much easier for the African males to handle.
column2: 不过，当我们得知有一个任务被设计出来，这个任务与肯德尔设计的任务非常相似，但非洲男性更容易完成时，这种现象便减弱了。
column4: on the other hand|另一方面

column1: Instead of the button-pressing machine, Cole used a locked box and two differently coloured match-boxes, one of which contained a key that would open the box.
column2: 与那种需要按按钮的机器不同，科尔使用了一个锁着的盒子，以及两个颜色不同的火柴盒，其中一个火柴盒里藏有一把钥匙，用这把钥匙就可以打开盒子。

column1: Notice that there are still two behaviour segments — ‘open the right match-box to get the key’ and ‘use the key to open the box’ – so the task seems formally to be the same.
column2: 请注意，仍然存在两个行为片段——‘打开正确的匹配盒以获取钥匙’和‘用钥匙打开盒子’——因此从形式上看，任务似乎相同。

column1: But psychologically it is quite different, Now the subject is dealing not with a strange machine but with familiar meaningful objects, and it is clear to him what he is meant to do.
column2: 但从心理层面来看，情况却大不相同。现在，主体所面对的不再是那些陌生的机器，而是那些熟悉且具有意义的物体，因此他清楚地知道自己应该做什么。

column1: It then turns out that the difficulty of ‘integration’ is greatly reduced.
column2: 结果表明，实现‘整合’的难度大大降低。

column1: Recent work by Simon Hewson is of great interest here for it shows that, for young children, too, the difficulty lies not in the inferential processes which the task demands, but in certain perplexing features of the apparatus and the procedure.
column2: 西蒙·休斯的最新研究极具兴趣，因为它表明，对于年幼儿童而言，困难并不在于任务所要求的推理过程，而在于实验装置和程序中某些令人费解的特征。

column1: When these are changed in ways which do not at all affect the inferential nature of the problem, then five-year-old children solve the problem as well as college students did in the Kendlers’ own experiments.
column2: 当实验装置和程序的改变不改变问题的推理性质时，五岁儿童解决问题的能力与大学学生在肯德尔实验中表现相当。

column1: Hewson made two crucial changes.
column2: 赫伍森做出了两项至关重要的调整。

column1: First, he replaced the button-pressing mechanism in the side panels by drawers in these panels which the child could open and shut.
column2: 首先，他用可开合的抽屉取代了侧板上的按钮装置，孩子可以自行打开和关闭这些抽屉。

column1: This took away the mystery from the first stage of training.
column2: 这消除了训练第一阶段的神秘感。

column1: Then he helped the child to understand that there was no ‘magic’ about the specific marble which, during the second stage of training, the experimenter handed to him so that he could pop it in the hole and get the reward.
column2: 然后，他帮助孩子理解：在训练的第二阶段中，实验者给他的那颗弹珠其实并没有什么‘神奇’之处——只要把弹珠放入相应的洞里，就能获得奖励。

column1: A child understands nothing, after all, about how a marble put into a hole can open a little door.
column2: 毕竟，孩子根本不懂把一颗弹珠放进洞里能打开一扇小门。

column1: How is he to know that any other marble of similar size will do just as well?
column2: 他怎么可能知道，其他尺寸相似的弹珠也能达到同样的效果呢？

column1: Yet he must assume that if he is to solve the problem.
column2: 不过，他必须假设，如果要想解决这个问题的话……

column1: Hewson made the functional equivalence of different marbles clear by playing a ‘swapping game’ with the children.
column2: 赫伍森通过和孩子们玩一个‘交换游戏’，清楚地说明了不同弹珠之间的功能等价性。

column1: The two modifications together produced a jump in success rates from 30 per cent to 90 per cent for five-year, the olds and from 35 per cent to 72.5 per cent for four-year-olds.
column2: 这两种改进措施共同作用后，五年龄儿童的成功率从30%提升到了90%，而四岁儿童的成功率则从35%上升到了72.5%。

column1: For three-year olds, for reasons that are still in need of clarification, no improvement — rather a slight drop in performance – resulted from the change.
column2: 对于三岁的儿童来说，由于一些尚未明确的原因，这种改变并没有带来任何进步——反而出现了轻微的性能下降。

column1: We may conclude, then, that children experience very real difficulty when faced with the Kendler apparatus; but this difficulty cannot be taken as proof that they are incapable of deductive reasoning.
column2: 因此，我们可以得出结论：儿童在面对肯德尔装置时确实会遇到真实困难，但这并不能证明他们不具备演绎推理能力。
